title: Lior and the Summer Revisited
premise: After a humiliating final concert ends his performing career, cellist Sebastian Vane retreats to his late aunt's orchard cottage on a fading island, intending to quietly sign the property over and vanish. But the deed bears a second name: Marisol Ferro, the woman he loved and abandoned fifteen years ago, now a lawyer who has returned to claim her half. As they're forced to renovate the orchard together before the deed can be divided—and before the last ferry of the season ends access—old truths surface, including the letter Sebastian never sent explaining why he left. At the orchard's harvest festival, Sebastian must choose between selling his half and fleeing to a safe, small life abroad, or staying to play again and love Marisol with his whole heart; he stays, and they rebuild the orchard, and his music, together.
about_author: Tamsin Crane is a former orchard worker turned novelist who writes love stories set in places where the tide dictates the schedule. She lives on a small island with a stubborn dog and an even more stubborn pear tree.

chapters.title: The Ferry That Almost Left Without Him
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He arrives on the island with a single suitcase and no cello, determined to sign away his aunt's cottage and disappear. A chance glimpse of a woman on the dock who resembles Marisol rattles him. Emotional beat: dread disguised as relief—he thinks he has finally escaped his past.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Deed
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the county office he discovers the orchard deed lists both him and Marisol Ferro as co-owners, an error—or a scheme—by his late aunt. He cannot sell without her signature. Emotional beat: panic; the past has followed him ashore.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Gate
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol arrives to claim her inheritance, equally stunned to find Sebastian living there. Their first confrontation crackles with fifteen years of silence. Emotional beat: anger that neither can sustain, because grief sits underneath it.

chapters.title: Ground Rules
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A lawyer forces them into cohabitation: neither may sell until the neglected orchard is appraised at fair value, requiring joint restoration before the season ends. Emotional beat: reluctant truce, laced with old intimacy neither admits to.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Clearing dead limbs, Marisol recalls the summer they fell in love under these trees—and the morning Sebastian vanished without explanation. Emotional beat: bittersweet nostalgia hardening into resolve not to be hurt twice.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Heart
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian unpacks his practice cello at night, unable to play more than a phrase. Flashbacks reveal his catastrophic final concert and the humiliation that ended his engagement to the orchestra. Emotional beat: shame; he lends out pieces of himself but never the whole.

chapters.title: Cider and Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Over pressed cider, Marisol, now a lawyer, interrogates Sebastian about the past; he deflects with charm that no longer works on her. Emotional beat: the first real laugh between them, immediately regretted.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm flattens the eastern rows; they work through the night salvaging what they can, hands brushing, walls lowering. Emotional beat: forced tenderness—the orchard makes them partners whether they like it or not.

chapters.title: The Letter He Never Sent
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian finds his aunt's safebox containing the unsent letter he wrote Marisol fifteen years ago explaining his departure. He burns it instead of reading it. Emotional beat: cowardice; the truth is now a live wire he refuses to touch.

chapters.title: An Offer from the Mainland
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol's old firm offers her a partnership in the city, contingent on returning within the month. She hides the offer from Sebastian. Emotional beat: the pull of duty versus the unfamiliar gravity of staying.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The community turns out for the harvest, and the town treats them as a couple. A neighbor's granddaughter asks Sebastian to teach her cello. Emotional beat: belonging sneaks up on him; the island sees him whole.

chapters.title: First Notes
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol overhears Sebastian teaching the child and then, alone at dusk, playing a full piece—the first time in years. Emotional beat: hope she doesn't dare name, and the ache of recognizing the man he might have become.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. After the harvest dinner they almost kiss; Sebastian pulls away, saying some things stay in the past tense. Marisol, wounded, decides to accept the mainland partnership. Emotional beat: heartbreak by self-sabotage.

chapters.title: Cold Storage
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Marisol's coldness mirrors the old wound; Sebastian realizes he is repeating the exact abandonment that broke them. He confides in the island's ferry captain, who knew his aunt. Emotional beat: the beginning of honesty, with the wrong person first.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The appraiser values the restored orchard high; the deed can now be divided. Freedom should feel like victory, but Marisol hesitates. Emotional beat: the terrifying discovery that she no longer wants the exit she came for.

chapters.title: What the Aunt Knew
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The ferry captain reveals Sebastian's aunt deliberately put both names on the deed—she knew Marisol's grandmother and wanted the families' story finished, not buried. Emotional beat: the past reinterpreted; his aunt was matchmaking from beyond.

chapters.title: The Other Letter
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol finds the aunt's copy of Sebastian's unsent letter and finally reads why he left: his father's bankruptcy and blackmail tied to her family, a sacrifice he made in secret. Emotional beat: fury and grief collapse into understanding at once.

chapters.title: The Confrontation at the Dock
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marisol confronts Sebastian as she's about to board the mainland ferry with the signed division papers. He confesses everything, including that he burned the letter out of shame. Emotional beat: the raw climax of truth—loyalty to old wounds versus the truth that frees them.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Marisol misses the ferry—by choice—and the two lay everything down: the concert disaster, the blackmail, the years apart. Emotional beat: surrender; the whole heart offered instead of pieces.

chapters.title: The Winter Concert
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sebastian agrees to play one public concert in the island chapel, his first performance since the catastrophe, with Marisol in the front row. Emotional beat: redemption through risk; hands steady, heart open.

chapters.title: One Deed, One Name
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They amend the deed to both names permanently, decline the mainland offer and the sale, and plant new rows for spring. Emotional beat: choosing belonging over safety, together.

chapters.title: Summer, Revisited
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Epilogue a year later: the orchard thrives, the child gives her first recital, and the first ferry of the season brings visitors to a couple who stayed. Emotional beat: quiet joy—love kept in the present tense at last.
